title: LatentRemedy: Efficient Remedy For Non-Prefix KV Cache Reuse in Multi-Agent Systems
summary: It replaces selective recomputation and offset-based calibration for recovering quality when reusing non-prefix KV cache blocks across agents with conflicting tasks, substituting recomputation of the shared block with a few MLP-generated latent tokens inserted after the reused block. The cost is training a small MLP via full-prefill distillation per model, plus extra inference-time compute and engineering to insert latent tokens into the serving path. It can fail outside multi-agent workloads with genuinely shared context blocks, if the distillation training does not transfer to a different base model or task distribution, or if the serving stack cannot accommodate inserted latent tokens without modification.
rationale: The method targets a narrow but real failure mode of cross-agent KV reuse and is deployable on a single GPU since it trains only a small MLP, but its benefit is workload-specific and requires integration and training effort, so small-scale validation is warranted before adoption.
technique: Latent token calibration for non-prefix KV cache reuse

claims.statement: It replaces selective recomputation and offset-based calibration for recovering quality when reusing non-prefix KV cache blocks across agents with conflicting tasks, substituting recomputation of the shared block with a few MLP-generated latent tokens inserted after the reused block. The cost is training a small MLP via full-prefill distillation per model, plus extra inference-time compute and engineering to insert latent tokens into the serving path. It can fail outside multi-agent workloads with genuinely shared context blocks, if the distillation training does not transfer to a different base model or task distribution, or if the serving stack cannot accommodate inserted latent tokens without modification.

Direct non-prefix KV reuse can degrade model performance by up to 90% on conflicting tasks; LatentRemedy consistently outperforms selective-recomputation and offset-based baselines while keeping TTFT close to direct reuse as cache size grows (no single quantified factor given).
